# Development and verification

## Editorial decisions

| Decision | Adopted approach |
|---|---|
| Audience | Researchers with basic R knowledge; statistical concepts explained as needed |
| Chapter sequence | Worked example, interpretation, assumptions and theory, implementation and limitations |
| R examples | Tidyverse style, native pipes, simple tables, and default `plot()` calls; automated assertions belong in development checks |
| Theory | Plain-language explanation first; define every symbol and explain each step of necessary equations |
| Derivations | Linked appendices |
| Public coverage | Every exported function, registered method, and scientifically distinct method option |
| Internal coverage | Scientific algorithms explained through numerical demonstrations; all named helpers indexed |
| Example context | Actual plant, animal, and human genotype datasets; human datasets for binary phenotypes; bring-your-own-data workflow first |
| Hosting | Static book suitable for GitHub Pages; publication requires a separate maintainer decision |

## Dataset strategy

The opening workflow starts with a reader's genotype file and supplies observed
maize genotypes as the reproducible example. Organism breadth means substantive
worked examples from different research communities, not artificial data with
species labels. Small constructed examples remain useful for checking algebra.

| Context | Role in the book | Current status |
|---|---|---|
| Plant | Maize input, continuous traits, crossing, selection, and breeding schemes | Bundled `SNP55K_maize282_maf04` (Cook et al. 2012; 280 inbred lines, 10,650 markers, MAF > 0.4 subset, synthetic map); used throughout |
| Animal | Relationship matrices, BLUP prediction, accuracy, and outbred allele frequencies | Heterogeneous-stock mice distributed with the BGLR package (`?BGLR::mice`, Valdar et al. 2006; 1,814 mice, 10,346 SNPs with physical positions); loaded by `_data.R` |
| Human | Binary phenotypes using the liability-threshold model; dominance on an outbred panel | HapMap Phase II subset distributed with SNPRelate (279 CEU, YRI, HCB and JPT individuals; 9,028 SNPs after dropping duplicated identifiers; missing calls imputed); loaded by `_data.R` |

Each dataset has documented provenance, redistribution through a CRAN or
Bioconductor package, and a reproducible route from the distributed files to the
chapter input (`docs/book/_data.R`, explained step by step in the
[genotype input chapter](input.qmd)). The human and mouse datasets travel with
their packages, so the book adds no data files of its own. The
[binary phenotype chapter](binary.qmd) distinguishes liability-scale parameters,
observed prevalence, and case/control sampling.

## Build the preview {#sec-build}

From a checkout with the package build dependencies, R, Python 3, and Quarto:

```{bash}
#| eval: false
Rscript --vanilla -e 'pkgload::load_all()'
quarto render docs/book
quarto preview docs/book
```

The R build dependencies include `pkgload`, `knitr`, `rmarkdown`, `jsonlite`, `dplyr`, `tibble`, `tidyr`, `readr`, `SNPRelate`, `gdsfmt`, and `BGLR`
(the last three supply the human and mouse datasets).
`dev/book/run_chapter.R` executes a single chapter's R chunks with knitr, without
Quarto, for a fast check while editing.
The package itself requires its declared R dependencies and the Rust toolchain.
The book's hidden setup loads this checkout, preventing an older installed
package from silently supplying the executed examples. Its visible examples use
ordinary `library(simplePHENOTYPES)` calls for readers with the matching version.

`dev/book/build_index.py` regenerates the function indexes, checks coverage
against `NAMESPACE`, verifies that referenced example labels exist, and copies
the archival equation map into the rendered resources. The generated indexes,
downloads, and HTML output are ignored by Git; the sources and coverage records
are maintained in the repository.

## Scientific review

For each scientific method, record its model assumptions, implemented expression,
primary source and verified page where applicable, numerical checks, and
independent review outcome. Algebraic derivations and package conventions must
be identified as such. An unverified literature page is never replaced by a guess.

The repository's `docs/THEORY_REVIEW.md` governs independent review before
commit. Passing example execution alone does not validate the theory.
Before publication, require complete example coverage, resolved scientific review,
successful book rendering, and a passing package test suite.

## Publication

The source lives under `docs/book/`, which is already excluded from the CRAN
package through the repository's `^docs$` build exclusion. The output directory
is `docs/book/_book/`; the existing `docs/` contents must not be overwritten by
rendered website files.

GitHub Pages can serve these static files from a Pages deployment artifact.
The preview workflow renders and uploads an artifact for inspection without
deploying it. Deployment will be configured after the book and its publication
scope have been reviewed. See the
[Quarto publishing guide](https://quarto.org/docs/publishing/github-pages.html).
